review_scope: Time_Delay_Normal tranche (branch codex/event-evaluator, tranche C1; issue #225): the Clause 13.3 pTimeDelayNormal parameter now exists as the Time_Delay_Normal property (identifier 356) on the nine intrinsic-reporting object types (AI/AO/AV/BI/BO/BV/MSI/MSO/MSV), and all three intrinsic event detectors (OutOfRange/ChangeOfState/CommandFailure, Clause 13.3.6/13.3.2/13.3.4) select the delay by transition direction: every indication into an OFFNORMAL state (including offnormal→offnormal re-indication) waits pTimeDelay; the sustained-condition return to NORMAL waits pTimeDelayNormal; an unwritten Time_Delay_Normal takes on Time_Delay's value per the parameter's fallback text, so absent behavior is byte-identical to the pre-tranche single-delay behavior. The property reads back the effective delay, is writable as Unsigned within the u32 span (every table carries it O-coded, so writability is permitted and mirrors Time_Delay - the #229 commissioning rationale), and is advertised in Property_List and the PICS writability truth source. FAULT transitions carry no delay (Clause 13.2.2 fault precedence, unchanged). Conventions unchanged: `repo_sha` names the last code commit of the PR branch (this docs-refresh commit lands after it), matching how the previous tranches recorded their reviewed SHA.

rows.requirement_summary: Server transaction state machine behavior, segmented request handling, SegmentACK behavior, and abort/reject mapping.
rows.notes: This slice adds server segmented ComplexAck send-side SegmentACK validation: SegmentACKs with the server bit set are ignored, positive ACKs advance only for the current segment, negative ACKs retransmit only the current requested segment, out-of-range negative ACKs are ignored, stale final ACKs do not complete the transfer, timeout retries retransmit before idle cleanup without a final timeout Abort, client Abort is routed to terminate the active segmented response without a spurious timeout Abort, routed SegmentACK/Abort events match the NPDU source-network key, segmented response frames set NPDU expecting_reply while waiting for SegmentACK, dispatch filters stale/future ACKs before queue insertion and does not block on a full SegmentACK queue, client Abort and same-peer/invoke-id replacement use nonblocking control events, live segmented sender tasks are capped by permits until each task exits, and replacement cancels the older sender so it cannot later emit a timeout Abort. The row remains below supported status pending a fuller server TSM transition audit, configured APDU segment timeout/retry exposure, and broader Reject/Error failure mapping coverage.

rows.requirement_summary: Only Confirmed-Request and ComplexACK may be segmented; SegmentACK windows and modulo-256 sequence handling are enforced.
rows.notes: This slice adds server ComplexAck send-side window evidence for current-sequence positive ACK advancement, first-window NAK0 retransmission, NAK of the previous sequence retransmitting the current segment, stale/future positive ACK ignore, wrong-direction ACK ignore, routed source-network matching, out-of-range NAK ignore, final ACK validation, timeout retransmission, repeated valid NAK abort, ACK flood/current-window filtering, and nonblocking full-queue SegmentACK dispatch. Remaining segmentation/window gaps include multi-segment window sizes beyond the current window-one send behavior, modulo-256 wrap, duplicate segment receive behavior, max APDU/max segment boundaries, and broader client/server receive-side out-of-order coverage.

rows.requirement_summary: Notification Class Recipient_List reads and writes use the Clause 21 BACnetDestination framing: seven application-tagged members in order (valid-days BACnetDaysOfWeek, from-time, to-time, recipient, process-identifier, issue-confirmed-notifications, transitions) concatenated as a BACnetLIST, with BACnetRecipient discriminated by context tag (device [0] primitive ObjectIdentifier, address [1] constructed BACnetAddress of application Unsigned16 + OCTET STRING).
rows.notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL; scope is the modeled NotificationClass path (NotificationForwarder's Recipient_List is a stub today). Golden vectors cover the device, address (nonzero network), and broadcast (zero-length MAC) forms; the 8-entry list round-trip covers the Annex K.2.25 AE-CRL-B minimum-entries posture. Decode is strict end to end: element sequence, fixed-width bit-string members (exactly one content octet with unused_bits 1 for valid-days / 5 for transitions), and whole-list routing (a malformed stored list fails closed with no prefix delivery). The write path and the routing filter share one flat-entry decoder, and the pre-#152 flat application-tagged form remains accepted there as a compatibility fallback. Indexed writes are rejected (Tranche K / #260 family). Remaining work: interop evidence against a second implementation and NotificationForwarder Recipient_List modeling.

rows.requirement_summary: Event_Parameters and Fault_Parameters read/write use the full Clause 21 ASN.1 CHOICE framing of BACnetEventParameter and BACnetFaultParameter: alternatives over SEQUENCEs as opening/closing context tag pairs with context-tagged members, explicitly tagged inner CHOICEs, fault-out-of-range inner CHOICEs discovered by application tag, and BACnetPropertyStates elements with the 135-2020 CHOICE tags.
rows.notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL. Evidence covers the modeled alternatives (change-of-bitstring/change-of-state/change-of-value/floating-limit/out-of-range/extended; all eight fault parameters) with golden vectors and round-trips, Opaque preservation of unmodeled alternatives (byte-for-byte for constructed forms; none [20] NULL decodes to Opaque{20, []} and re-encodes constructed), rejection of omitted/deprecated/reserved tags 6/7/12/19, rejection of trailing garbage after a framed element, property-state goldens, and the legacy flat + OctetString-to-Opaque write fallback retained per #129; unmodeled Opaques never reach the legacy little-endian evaluator. The framed property-state codec uses 135-2020 CHOICE tags which correct invented pre-2020 tags for door/timer/lift variants; the older BACnetNotificationParameters codec in bacnet-services still uses the old tags for those variants -- reconciling it is follow-up work with its own wire change (out of this row's scope).

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 12.17 Table 12-20 footnote 7 (Loop); Clause 12 Out_Of_Service property texts (12.2/12.3/12.4/12.6/12.7/12.8/12.19/12.21/12.22 families); Clause 12.24 Schedule Reliability_Evaluation_Inhibit text; Clause 12.25 Table 12-29 and Clause 12.30 Table 12-35 (Trend Log / Trend Log Multiple); Clause 21 BACnetReliability
rows.requirement_summary: On object types carrying Out_Of_Service and Reliability, Reliability is network-writable exactly when Out_Of_Service is TRUE (the simulation grant quoted in each carrier's Out_Of_Service property text), and the written value is validated against the BACnetReliability production: the named set derived from Reliability::ALL_NAMED (enumerated 0..=25 with 11 reserved for a future addendum) plus the vendor-proprietary range 64..=65535, refusing anything else with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE. In-service writes refuse PROPERTY / WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED (Clause 15.9.1.3 row: the property is currently not writable by the requestor). The evaluated value is saved on the FALSE-to-TRUE edge and restored on the TRUE-to-FALSE edge; the internal set_reliability_internal route carries the complementary ownership guard (refused while Out_Of_Service is TRUE). Trend Log and Trend Log Multiple, whose Reliability_Evaluation_Inhibit paragraphs end at 'shall have the value NO_FAULT_DETECTED.' without the out-of-service write provision, refuse all network Reliability writes.
rows.notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#240, #252). The nine intrinsic-reporting carriers were proven by #218/#239; this tranche added Loop as the tenth reliability_gate_test! carrier and Schedule as the eleventh, extended the predicate from a restated literal to a derivation from Reliability::ALL_NAMED (exhaustive 0..=65536 equivalence sweep; the value past the enum ceiling flips to accepted exactly when its addendum constant lands), and ran the sweep over the remaining OOS+Reliability carriers per #240: Schedule's Reliability_Evaluation_Inhibit text anticipates the out-of-service client write ('...unless Out_Of_Service is TRUE and an alternate value has been written to the Reliability property') so the gate applies with an internal route reserved for its CONFIGURATION_ERROR evaluation; Trend Log (Reliability O, Table 12-29) and Trend Log Multiple (Reliability O, Table 12-35) carry no writability footnote and no simulation-write provision, so the previously-accepting Trend Log arm now refuses PROPERTY / WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED (behavior change) and Trend Log Multiple's default denial is pinned as deliberate. Loop and Schedule also gained is_writable_property overrides mirroring their write arms so the PICS and runtime dispatch share one truth source. Residue: carriers that never grew a write arm (Lighting Output family, elevator/access-zone family) deny by default; whether each one's Clause 12 Out_Of_Service text obliges the writability half of its footnote is untriaged and tracked separately from this gate.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 12.3 Table 12-3 (Analog Output), Clause 12.7 Table 12-8 (Binary Output), Clause 12.8 Table 12-10 (Binary Value), Clause 12.19 Table 12-22 (Multi-state Output), Clause 12.20 Table 12-23 (Multi-state Value), Clause 12.26 Table 12-30 (Access Door), Clause 12.54 Table 12-64 (Lighting Output), Clause 12.55 Table 12-69 (Binary Lighting Output), Clause 12 value object tables; Clause 19 command prioritization
rows.requirement_summary: Relinquish_Default is network-writable and locally settable on the commandable object types, where the conformance tables carry it R or O and writability is permitted, not required - this row records permitted writability implemented, not a conformance upgrade. Each arm routes through a validated local set_relinquish_default and re-resolves Present_Value from the priority array afterward, so an all-NULL array falls back to the new default immediately while a live command still outranks it. Validation mirrors the Present_Value path per type: finite Real (AO/AV), BinaryPV 0/1 (BO/BV), Unsigned 1..=Number_Of_States (MSO/MSV), finite Real in 0..=100 (Lighting Output), BinaryLightingPV 0..=4 (Binary Lighting Output), the BACnetDoorValue production 0..=3 - lock, unlock, pulse-unlock, extended-pulse-unlock (Access Door), and per-type extraction bounds plus a finite check for the Large Analog Value (Double). With #182 the datetime-paired value types (DateTime Value, Clause 12.38 Table 12-45; DateTime Pattern Value, Clause 12.46) join the network-writable set: the BACnetDateTime pair decodes from application-tagged Date+Time in the multi-element service decode.
rows.notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#270). is_commandable_property_writable now advertises RELINQUISH_DEFAULT for the six core commandable types (its doc no longer claims universal read-only); Lighting Output, Binary Lighting Output, Access Door, and the define_value_object_commandable! macro gained is_writable_property overrides mirroring their write arms - the macro override also corrects the PRIORITY_ARRAY writability advertising for all twelve commandable value types (previously reported read-only by the historical default while the arm accepted writes). Invalid writes refuse with the Present_Value arm's pairings (VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE for range/finiteness, INVALID_DATA_TYPE for a wrong BACnet datatype) and leave both Relinquish_Default and Present_Value untouched. Number_Of_States shrink interplay on MSO/MSV: Clause 12.19/12.22 leave stored-value adjustment a local matter and this implementation does not auto-adjust - pinned in a test comment, with CONFIGURATION_ERROR reporting for the condition tracked under #226. CURRENT_COMMAND_PRIORITY stays read-only (derived). The pre-existing unvalidated Present_Value arm on Access Door (any Enumerated accepted) is a separate defect noted for follow-up, as is the door property_list omitting PRIORITY_ARRAY/RELINQUISH_DEFAULT while both are readable. #182 addendum: the `readonly` rd_access selection now has no users (kept in the macro for a future type whose wire form needs something the service decode cannot deliver); the pinned-denial test datetime_value_relinquish_default_is_not_network_writable is replaced by datetime_value_relinquish_default_write_recaptures_present_value.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 12.17 with Table 12-20 (Loop), Clause 12.23 with Table 12-27 (Pulse Converter Input_Reference), Clause 12.5 Table 12-5 (Averaging Object_Property_Reference - BACnetDeviceObjectPropertyReference), Clause 21 BACnetObjectPropertyReference / BACnetSetpointReference productions
rows.requirement_summary: The Loop Controlled_Variable_Reference, Manipulated_Variable_Reference, and Setpoint_Reference properties (Clause 12.17) and the Pulse Converter Input_Reference (Clause 12.23) are typed BACnetObjectPropertyReference - a SEQUENCE of primitive context-tagged members [0]/[1] plus optional property-array-index [2] - with Setpoint_Reference nested [0] inside the BACnetSetpointReference production. Network writes now land in these wire forms through the multi-element service decode: a strict typed codec (bacnet-encoding/src/constructed/object_property_reference.rs) requires full consumption and rejects a device-qualifying member [3], since unlike BACnetDeviceObjectPropertyReference these references are local-device only. Each arm also keeps the legacy local list form [ObjectIdentifier, Enumerated, Unsigned?] in exact shape, with the property-id member accepted as Unsigned OR Enumerated (the Averaging flat form carries Unsigned, the Loop/Pulse form Enumerated; both decode to the same reference). The Averaging arm - typed BACnetDeviceObjectPropertyReference by Table 12-5, whose remote-sample path is the standard's OPTIONAL branch and unmodeled here - routes through the same shared decode (review-round blocker fix), and the BACnetSetpointReference frame with its OPTIONAL member absent clears Setpoint_Reference exactly like a Null write (review-round runtime/dataflow item).
rows.notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#182). The four arms share one objects-layer helper (reference.rs) so the local List form (in-process compatibility) and the framed ApplicationData form (network) converge on the same strict Clause 21 decode; error pairings follow Clause 15.9.1.3: wrong value datatype is PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_TYPE, malformed framing / device qualification / unknown trailing context tag is PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_ENCODING, and a mixed flat+framed element list is refused rather than reinterpreted. Null clears, and read arms carry the reference's optional array index as a third list element. Setpoint_Reference additionally accepts the BACnetSetpointReference opening/closing tag [0] frame (unambiguous against the bare form's leading primitive [0]) while refusing unbalanced frames. WritePropertyMultiple in-order commit and rollback are proven for a reference+setpoint request failing its second property. Review round: the adversary lane's blocker on the Averaging arm (silent member drop / member retype / as-u32 truncation, newly network-reachable) is fixed by routing it through the same shared decode; the runtime+dataflow empty-frame finding is fixed by the Option-returning decode_setpoint_reference; the dataflow PICS incoherence is fixed by exact is_writable_property overrides on Pulse Converter (PRESENT_VALUE / SCALE_FACTOR / ADJUST_VALUE / INPUT_REFERENCE + DESCRIPTION / OUT_OF_SERVICE / COV_INCREMENT) and Averaging (OBJECT_PROPERTY_REFERENCE + DESCRIPTION / OUT_OF_SERVICE), which also stop advertising OBJECT_NAME on both types (no arm routes it - a truth-toward-arms PICS correction). Limitation: reads still emit the flat application-tagged list form rather than re-framing context tags - the encode side is unchanged by this tranche; interop evidence against a second implementation remains open.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 13.3.2 CHANGE_OF_STATE, Clause 13.3.4 COMMAND_FAILURE, Clause 13.3.6 OUT_OF_RANGE (pTimeDelayNormal definitions and condition letters); Clause 12.2 Table 12-2 (Analog Input, O5), 12.3 Table 12-3 (Analog Output, O4), 12.4 Table 12-4 (Analog Value, O6), 12.6 Table 12-6 (Binary Input, O7), 12.7 Table 12-8 (Binary Output, O6), 12.8 Table 12-10 (Binary Value, O8), 12.18 Table 12-21 (Multi-state Input, O5), 12.19 Table 12-22 (Multi-state Output, O3), 12.20 Table 12-23 (Multi-state Value, O6)
rows.requirement_summary: Time_Delay_Normal (property identifier 356) is the pTimeDelayNormal parameter of the object's event algorithm on the nine intrinsic-reporting object types. All indications into OFFNORMAL event states - including offnormal-to-offnormal re-indication (Clause 13.3.2 (c), 13.3.6 (d)/(g)) - wait pTimeDelay; the sustained-condition return to NORMAL waits pTimeDelayNormal (13.3.2 (b), 13.3.4 (b), 13.3.6 (e)/(h)); and "If no value is available for this parameter, then it takes on the value of the pTimeDelay parameter", so the absent case is symmetric by construction. The property reads back the effective delay (Time_Delay before any write), is writable as Unsigned within the u32 span with the Clause 15.9.1.3 pairings on refusal (wrong datatype is PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_TYPE, unrepresentable is PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE), and is advertised in Property_List and the PICS writability truth source, mirroring Time_Delay. FAULT transitions carry no delay (Clause 13.2.2 fault precedence).

crates/bacnet-objects/src/multistate/tests/generic_event_properties.rs (TIME_DELAY_NORMAL in the shared round-trip helper: MSI/MSV/MSO)

rows.notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#225). Direction selection lives once in event.rs (`delay_toward`) and feeds every probe/tick seeding site; mid-delay re-seed uses the CURRENT target's delay, and condition-revert cancellation is unchanged (a revert to the confirmed state leaves nothing pending - staying in the confirmed state is not a new indication). Detector and object constructors keep Time_Delay_Normal absent (`None`) so default behavior equals the normative fallback, never an error. Conformance-code verification against the local text extract (whose two-column page-break interleave was a known alignment risk): each table's property/datatype pairs were counted against its conformance-code count (AI 42-42 with Time_Delay=O3,5 at extract line 11845 and Time_Delay_Normal=O5 at 11860; AO 45-45; AV 44-44; BI 37-37; BV 44-44; MSI 37-37; MSV 39-39), MSO Table 12-22 read in exact name/type/code triples (Time_Delay=O1,3 at 19377-19379, Time_Delay_Normal=O3 at 19412-19414), and every O-coded footnote body confirmed as 'These properties shall be present only if the object supports intrinsic reporting' adjacent to its footnote number (extract 11888-11889, 12333-12334, 12819-12820, 13555-13556, 14078-14079, 14650-14651, 19019-19020, 19473 with the '3' marker lost to the interleave but pinned by the EAI=O3,4 and REI=O5 code cross-checks, 19939-19940). No table marks Time_Delay_Normal writable (W); acceptance mirrors Time_Delay (#229 rationale: otherwise the delay asymmetry is not commissionable). Reset semantics mirror Time_Delay: the EDE=FALSE restoration path does not touch either delay, and none was invented. Limitation (pre-existing, deferred to the evaluator tranche): OUT_OF_RANGE's no-delay returns on a limit being disabled (13.3.6 (c)/(f)) are not separately modeled - a LIMIT_ENABLE write that disables an active limit still returns through the deadband path gated by pTimeDelayNormal.

rows.requirement_summary: Server-side COV subscription procedures validate subscription inputs, preserve subscriber endpoints, emit initial COV notifications after accepted SubscribeCOV, SubscribeCOVProperty, and SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple requests, and preserve notification service family on later changes.
rows.notes: Issue #82 evidence adds post-acceptance initial notifications for SubscribeCOV and SubscribeCOVProperty, COVNotificationMultiple APDUs with the multiple service choices for SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple initial and later-change notifications, property-validation and subscription-capacity atomicity, routed subscriber endpoint preservation for SimpleAck, notification sends, and segmented ComplexAck responses, subscriber COV increment precedence, and server TSM invoke-ID collision avoidance for routed/confirmed notifications. Issue #83 evidence adds SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple request lifetime encoding/decoding in the standard field order, mandatory issue-confirmed validation, paired lifetime/max-delay validation, cancellation handling for empty contexts and listed property specs, context lifetime refresh, and server-side subscription expiration from the decoded lifetime. This row remains below supported status until fuller BIBB/PICS and clause-level conformance evidence exists, including first-failed-subscription response shape, complete Device active-COV property synchronization, context-level Active_COV_Multiple_Subscriptions evidence, and fuller clause-level evidence.

rows.requirement_summary: ReadProperty, ReadPropertyMultiple, WriteProperty, and WritePropertyMultiple reject an array index supplied for a property that is not a BACnetARRAY with PROPERTY / PROPERTY_IS_NOT_AN_ARRAY, applying the per-object BACnetARRAY/BACnetLIST classification of Clause 12.1.5 (a BACnetLIST admits positional access only through ReadRange, Clause 12.1.5.2); true BACnetARRAY properties keep their index semantics.
rows.notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#190, #260, #266). The gate is one query on the object (BACnetObject::is_array_property, default keyed by the Clause 12 object tables) so the classification cannot drift between services: identifier-stable BACnetARRAY properties modeled in-tree (OBJECT_LIST Table 12-13, PROPERTY_LIST, STATE_TEXT Tables 12-21/12-22/12-23, PRIORITY Table 12-24, WEEKLY_SCHEDULE/EXCEPTION_SCHEDULE Table 12-28, EVENT_TIME_STAMPS/EVENT_MESSAGE_TEXTS Table 12-2 family, PRIORITY_ARRAY, TAGS Annex Y, SUBORDINATE_LIST/SUBORDINATE_ANNOTATIONS Table 12-34, GROUP_MEMBERS/GROUP_MEMBER_NAMES Table 12-57, ACTION Table 12-12, STAGES/STAGE_NAMES/TARGET_REFERENCES Table 12-80) admit an index; identifier-stable BACnetLIST properties (DATE_LIST Table 12-11, LIST_OF_GROUP_MEMBERS Table 12-17, RECIPIENT_LIST Table 12-24, LOG_BUFFER Tables 12-29/12-31, DEVICE_ADDRESS_BINDING and ACTIVE_COV_SUBSCRIPTIONS Table 12-13) and all scalars reject it; the type-dependent identifiers classify by object type (ALARM_VALUES/FAULT_VALUES array on CharacterString/BitString Value per Tables 12-44/12-47 but list on the multi-state/life-safety/access families, LIST_OF_OBJECT_PROPERTY_REFERENCES array on Channel per Table 12-62 but list on Schedule/Timer per Tables 12-28/12-75, PRESENT_VALUE BACnetARRAY on Global Group per Table 12-57). Array-typed identifiers whose object types are not modeled in-tree (ACTION_TEXT, EVENT_MESSAGE_TEXTS_CONFIG, VALUE_SOURCE_ARRAY, ...) stay rejected until their object-side modeling lands, so coverage is complete for the modeled set rather than for every array in the standard. The RP whitelist that admitted six always-list identifiers is gone; RPM gates per reference with inline error elements while siblings succeed; WP gates before decode/mutation; WPM gates in the validation phase so the commit loop never starts (mixed valid+gated requests commit nothing, proven by test). Indexed Recipient_List reads and writes fail with the same gate classification — mirrored at the object layer for direct calls — replacing the tranche-J INVALID_DATA_TYPE stopgap. #266: omitted-index (whole-array, Clause 12.1.5.1) Priority_Array writes are PROPERTY / WRITE_ACCESS_DENIED (a mappable Result(-)) while indexes 0 and 17 stay INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX; pinned at both macro sites and over the network WP/WPM paths. Limitations: the gate controls index admissibility only — object-side element semantics for Global Group / Channel / Structured View / Command / Staging arrays still return whole values (#171-family residue), and CharacterString/BitString Value ALARM_VALUES/FAULT_VALUES are gate-classified as arrays but not yet modeled (an accepted index surfaces UNKNOWN_PROPERTY). Refs #171: its service-gating half landed; the TimeStamp CHOICE and element-datatype residue stays open.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 15.9.1.3 (WriteProperty error table) with Clause 21 BACnetNotifyType / BACnetEventTransitionBits / BACnetLimitEnable productions
rows.requirement_summary: WriteProperty validation of the shared intrinsic-reporting event properties matches the Clause 15.9.1.3 error semantics: Notify_Type (BACnetNotifyType, a closed {alarm, event, ack-notification} production) refuses out-of-production values with PROPERTY / VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE ('The value provided is outside the range of values that the property can take on'), and Event_Enable / Limit_Enable (BACnetEventTransitionBits = 3 bits, BACnetLimitEnable = 2 bits) require the canonical encoding of their fixed-width production - exactly one content octet with 8-N declared unused bits, the form the read path emits - refusing any other shape with PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_ENCODING ('The encoding is not valid for the datatype of the property'). A previously-silent normalization of an over-long bit string (masking its first octet and dropping the declared count) is now a refusal, as is an empty content (previously INVALID_DATA_TYPE). Notify_Type membership derives from NotifyType::ALL_NAMED so a future addendum constant widens the gate without a second edit.
rows.notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#255; behavior change - previously-accepted invalid writes now fail). The generic macro arms cover AI/AO/AV/BI/BO/BV/MSI/MSO/MSV, the analog macro arm adds Limit_Enable, and the EventEnrollment and AlertEnrollment objects carry their own arms with identical validation. A shared objects-layer helper (common::check_fixed_width_bit_string) shapes the PROPERTY-class error; the decoding-layer sibling in bacnet-encoding is intentionally not reused across layers. Covered shapes: out-of-production Notify_Type (3, 99, u32::MAX), an 8-bit string where the production defines fewer bits, extra or missing content octets, a half-octet string, and - for Limit_Enable - the valid Event_Enable 3-bit shape, which must not cross-apply. Related unaddressed family: the Notification Class recipient-list decoder still masks transition/day bit strings without consulting declared counts - noted as a follow-up rather than folded into this tranche.

rows.standard_anchor: Clause 15.9 WriteProperty (15.9.1.2 Result(+), 15.9.1.3 Result(-)), Clause 15.10 WritePropertyMultiple, Clause 20.2.1 (concatenated elements)
rows.requirement_summary: WriteProperty and WritePropertyMultiple decode the entire propertyValue payload: elements are decoded with decode_application_value until the input is exhausted - the mirror of encode_property_value's List flattening - so one element yields the scalar PropertyValue and more than one yields PropertyValue::List. Full consumption is required: a partial or undecodable trailing element, and an empty payload, are PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_ENCODING per Clause 15.9.1.3 (The encoding is not valid for the datatype of the property) - never a silent drop - with the stored value proven unchanged; a well-formed extra element reaches a scalar arm and fails its shape as INVALID_DATA_TYPE. The RECIPIENT_LIST verbatim special-case keeps its precedence and the context-tagged ApplicationData widening of the single-element decoder is preserved (framed CHOICE properties, Clause 12.17 reference members).
rows.notes: Split child of BACNET-12-OBJECT-MODEL (#182; behavior change - trailing bytes previously dropped between the single-element decoder and the arm now decide the write, and malformed value payloads map to PROPERTY / INVALID_DATA_ENCODING instead of the SERVICES/OTHER a propagated raw decoding error produced). A value TLV-truncated far enough to break framing is refused earlier by the service request's own [3]/[4] context walk (a framing error, still never silent; pinned by list_write_with_tlv_truncated_tail_is_refused_before_the_value_decode). Unlocks covered here: MSI Alarm_Values whole-list writes (the pin in handlers/list.rs flipped from pinned failure to per-element-validated success) and the datetime-paired value properties completing #270 (DateTime Value PV / Priority_Array entries, Relinquish_Default on DateTime Value + DateTime Pattern Value; see BACNET-12-RELINQUISH-DEFAULT-WRITABILITY). WPM keeps its validate-all-then-commit-with-rollback semantics for structured values. Known residues (follow-ups, not regressions): AddListElement/RemoveListElement still break their listOfElements loop on an undecodable element instead of erroring (#182's wider scope); Enumerated contents wider than four octets still truncate to u32 (#277, explicitly untouched); and properties declared SEQUENCE OF beyond the four reference arms (e.g. LIST_OF_OBJECT_PROPERTY_REFERENCES) keep their pre-existing arm-level behavior.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet encoding, application tags, constructed data, and malformed encoding behavior are validated.
rows.notes: Needs a complete malformed fixture catalog and byte-equivalence guard for optimizations.

rows.requirement_summary: Formal APDU structures, service choices, errors, rejects, aborts, and confirmed/unconfirmed service encodings are validated.
rows.notes: Needs service-by-service fixture coverage in later PRs.

rows.requirement_summary: All BACnetTimeStamp producers and consumers share one codec: time [0] as a primitive context tag 0 of length 4 holding raw Time octets, sequence-number [1] constrained to Unsigned (0..65535) and enforced on encode and decode, datetime [2] as an opening/closing tag 2 pair around application-tagged Date and Time, in both bare-CHOICE (SEQUENCE OF member) and field-wrapped forms.
rows.notes: Split child of BACNET-21-FORMAL-APDUS. Resolves the divergent dual-codec defect from #259 per the Clause 20.2.1 tag-form rules: time [0] tags the primitive base type Time, so the primitives codec's primitive-tag form is conformant and the GetEventInformationAck opening-tag-0 form was removed. Golden vectors, 0/65535 boundary acceptance, 65536 and 3-octet overflow rejection, and a cross-call-site primitives<->GetEventInformationAck matrix all run in-tree.

rows.requirement_summary: PICS output is generated as draft internal support evidence until formal BTL/PICS evidence exists.
rows.notes: This ledger does not claim certification.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/IPv4 BVLC type, Annex J.2 function code, length handling, and BVLC-Result result-code parsing are table-tested, with deleted-value passthrough tracked separately.
rows.notes: J-01 covers Annex J.2 function constants through 0x0B, representative frames, wrong type, short/overlong declared lengths, unknown function passthrough, and current decoder policy for bytes beyond the declared BVLC Length. J-02 adds exact two-byte BVLC-Result parsing, unknown result-code passthrough, malformed result rejection, and sender/expected-function correlation for pending management responses. SECURE_BVLL 0x0C is tested only as deleted-value passthrough. J-13 adds reproducible local and base/head benchmark runners for BIP Criterion suites with ignored raw artifacts and a machine-readable result-row schema. BBMD/FDT lifecycle semantics remain for later J-03 work.

rows.requirement_summary: Original-Unicast-NPDU frames preserve exact BVLC length, payload validation, and source/reply semantics.
rows.notes: Generic BVLL envelope coverage exists. J-04 Original-NPDU evidence covers UDP sender B/IP MAC delivery to the upper layer and self-originated frame suppression. Directed reply-path integration remains open.

rows.requirement_summary: Original-Broadcast-NPDU frames are encoded, decoded, and routed according to BACnet/IP broadcast semantics.
rows.notes: Generic BVLL envelope coverage exists. J-04 Original-NPDU evidence covers BBMD handling of Original-Broadcast-NPDU: local delivery uses sender B/IP MAC, remote BDT peer and registered FDT targets receive Forwarded-NPDU with the original sender encoded, and the BBMD does not echo the already-local broadcast back onto the local subnet as Forwarded-NPDU. J-09 adds platform socket evidence for Annex J local broadcast prerequisites: the B/IP socket binds INADDR_ANY for subnet/limited-broadcast reception while retaining the configured interface in the local B/IP MAC, and SO_BROADCAST is enabled for Original-Broadcast-NPDU sends. J-10 adds B/IP send-path evidence that Clause 6 global-broadcast and remote-broadcast NPDUs preserve DNET, DLEN 0 broadcast DADR, Hop Count, and APDU bytes unchanged inside Annex J Original-Broadcast-NPDU. Additional malformed/unsupported-path coverage remains open.

rows.requirement_summary: Forwarded-NPDU includes a valid originating BACnet/IP MAC and preserves source-address semantics.
rows.notes: J-04 covers generic originating-address parsing, truncated-address rejection, BBMD delivery with originating B/IP source MAC, FDT fanout preserving the origin, local rebroadcast for unicast peer arrivals, directed-broadcast peer local-rebroadcast suppression, and no onward forwarding to other BDT peers. Original-Broadcast fanout covers BDT/FDT Forwarded-NPDU emission with original sender preservation and no local echoed Forwarded-NPDU. Non-BDT Forwarded-NPDU evidence verifies rejection before local delivery, local rebroadcast, BDT fanout, or FDT fanout. DBTN evidence covers registered foreign-device fanout to local broadcast, BDT peer, and non-origin FDT peer while preserving the origin, excluding origin echo, checking for no extra duplicate frames, and returning X'0060' when deterministic local Forwarded-NPDU forwarding fails.

rows.requirement_summary: BBMD Broadcast Distribution Table write/read/ACK behavior and peer broadcast fanout are validated.
rows.notes: J-03 covers read/write BDT caller paths, replacement semantics, malformed Write-BDT NAK without table mutation, self-entry insertion without overflow, and directed-broadcast forwarding target calculation. J-04 adds Forwarded-NPDU BDT mask behavior: full-mask peers require local rebroadcast, directed-broadcast and unknown peers skip it, Forwarded-NPDUs are not forwarded onward to other BDT peers, and non-BDT senders are rejected before BDT fanout. Original-Broadcast fanout covers one remote BDT target and verifies no local Forwarded-NPDU echo. DBTN fanout covers a registered foreign-device request forwarded to a BDT peer plus local broadcast and FDT targets without extra duplicate frames. J-07 adds project ACL evidence for the legacy Write-BDT path: listed management senders can update the table, and unlisted senders receive the standard Write-BDT NAK without table mutation. J-08 adds BDT persistence evidence: successful Write-BDT stores the current wire-format BDT for restart load, and invalid persisted bytes fall back to the configured BDT without accepting malformed state. J-11 adds client-side Read-Broadcast-Distribution-Table-Ack validation that rejects malformed payload lengths not divisible by the Annex J.2.4 N*10 BDT entry size. J-12 adds raw BBMD Read-Broadcast-Distribution-Table-Ack wire evidence for ACK function code and N*10 BDT entry bytes. J-13 adds reproducible BBMD stress benchmark A/B runner evidence with ignored raw artifacts and a machine-readable result-row schema.

rows.requirement_summary: Foreign-device registration, TTL bounds, re-registration, read/delete FDT, expiry, and DBTN authorization are validated.
rows.notes: J-03 covers FDT read/register/delete caller paths, re-registration, zero-TTL and malformed TTL NAKs, exact Delete-FDT payload length, max TTL remaining-time capping, expiry purge, source exclusion, and unregistered DBTN NAK without local delivery. J-04 Original-Broadcast evidence covers fanout to one registered foreign device while preserving the original sender in the Forwarded-NPDU. DBTN evidence covers registered origin plus peer FDT fanout, preserves the original foreign-device B/IP source, verifies no echo to the originating foreign device, checks for no extra duplicate FDT frames, and verifies a registered origin receives X'0060' when forwarding cannot be completed. Non-BDT Forwarded-NPDU evidence verifies no FDT fanout. J-06 adds a BBMD-owned timer purge task for Annex J.5.2.3, covers expiration without an inbound BVLC request, and covers re-registration resetting the entry before the purge task removes it. J-07 adds project ACL evidence for Delete-FDT: listed management senders can delete registered entries, and unlisted senders receive the standard Delete-FDT NAK without removing the entry. J-11 adds client-side Read-Foreign-Device-Table-Ack validation that rejects malformed payload lengths not divisible by the Annex J.2.8 N*10 FDT entry size. J-12 adds raw BBMD Read-Foreign-Device-Table-Ack wire evidence for ACK function code and N*10 FDT entry fields. J-13 adds reproducible foreign-device/BBMD stress benchmark A/B runner evidence with ignored raw artifacts and a machine-readable result-row schema.

rows.requirement_summary: NAT-supporting BBMD operation is optional, but a support claim requires global B/IP address configuration, port-forwarding assumptions, Forwarded-NPDU originating-address rewrite, and two-hop distribution evidence.
rows.notes: Current IPv4 B/IP surfaces expose interface, port, broadcast address, BDT/FDT management, and foreign-device registration, but no reviewed global B/IP address field, NAT mode flag, BBMD/router logical-port model, or non-received Forwarded-NPDU originating-address rewrite for NAT. Existing BDT full-mask behavior covers two-hop fanout mechanics, but not Annex J.7.5 NAT traversal as a product claim. No public NAT traversal claim is made. Follow-up work item 019f0ff8-14c0-7013-9721-3bc5fe0356de tracks an owner decision and implementation plan if support is later claimed.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/IP multicast (B/IP-M) support requires IPv4 multicast group configuration, Original-Broadcast-NPDU multicast delivery, BBMD membership in the group, and two-hop BDT behavior for B/IP-M BBMD peers.
rows.notes: Current IPv4 B/IP transport sends local broadcasts to a configured IPv4 broadcast address and does not expose B/IP-M multicast group membership, multicast send, or B/IP-M BBMD group configuration. BACnet/IPv6 multicast code and README/docs wording are Annex U evidence only and do not satisfy Annex J.8 B/IP-M. No public Annex J IPv4 multicast claim is made. Follow-up work item 019f0ff8-14e7-7681-8738-032683da62df tracks an owner decision and implementation plan if support is later claimed.

rows.notes: Detailed BIBB rows should be generated from service-specific evidence in later work.

rows.requirement_summary: Device profile support is derived from ledger/PICS evidence and remains draft until formal validation.
rows.notes: No profile certification claim is made by this seed.

rows.requirement_summary: ZigBee data-link support status is classified with source evidence.
rows.notes: No public support claim found in the initial scan.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/IPv6 BVLC function codes, address handling, and multicast scope behavior are validated.
rows.notes: Needs Annex U-specific malformed frame and multicast-scope tests.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC BVLC-SC frame function, control, options, VMAC, and payload validation.
rows.notes: AB-01 adds transport codec evidence for Annex AB.2 control flag bits 7..4 rejection, Header Option Type 1..31 enforcement, AB.2.17 destination/data option marker decoding, VMAC field ordering, option count cap enforcement, option length truncation, option data truncation, and unterminated option-chain rejection. Addenda 135-2020cf/cp were checked for this row: cf renames Data Options bit 6 to Every Segment without changing the marker bit position, and cp adds standard header option types 2..5 that remain accepted by the generic 1..31 parser. Broader non-Result BVLC-SC function-specific payload semantics, destination-option Must Understand NAK behavior, Every Segment segmentation behavior, and hub/direct-connection behavior remain for later Annex AB work.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC BVLC-Result ACK/NAK payload parsing and connection handling.
rows.notes: AB-02 adds typed BVLC-Result ACK/NAK payload parsing for transport. ACK fixtures use the Proprietary-Message function per addendum 135-2020ci, while NAK fixtures mirror AB.2.17 examples with and without UTF-8 Error Details, including the Figure AB-6 multibyte UTF-8 details bytes. Negative evidence covers ACK trailing fields, short NAKs, unknown result codes, invalid UTF-8 details, malformed empty payloads, Data Options absence, Connect-Request NAK failing before timeout, fatal Result NAK closing the receive loop before further heartbeats, and malformed wire-level Result decode failures closing without a Result response. Transport connection handling now keeps ACK benign, disconnects on NAK, and disconnects on malformed Result without generating a Result response. Negotiated Max-BVLC-Length resource-limit evidence is tracked under BACNET-AB-SC-CONNECTION-STATE. Remaining work includes request correlation, Error Details resource limits, standard-function ACK diagnostic policy, BVLC-Result generation for every AB.3.1.5 error situation, destination-option Must Understand NAK behavior, and hub/direct response-routing behavior.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC Data Options are exposed to the network layer as data_attributes and handled explicitly across supported SC/non-SC boundaries.
rows.notes: This row now has native receive-side, outbound send, router local-delivery, router forwarding, and unsupported Must Understand fail-closed evidence for BACnet/SC Encapsulated-NPDU Data Options. Receive paths convert supported or non-Must-Understand Data Options into generic transport DataAttribute values, preserving option type, Must Understand flag, and option data on ReceivedNpdu; NetworkLayer exposes those attributes on ReceivedApdu after NPDU decode; router local-delivery paths retain inbound attributes; router forwarding attaches inbound attributes to forwarded unicast and broadcast SendRequest values; and non-SC transports emit empty data_attributes on receive. Native SC treats valid Secure Path Data Option type 1 as understood, rejects other Must Understand Data Options before NPDU delivery, returns BVLC-Result NAK COMMUNICATION/HEADER_NOT_UNDERSTOOD with the offending option marker for non-broadcast traffic, drops broadcast traffic without a result, and preserves unsupported non-Must-Understand Data Options as DataAttribute values. Outbound paths add attribute-aware TransportPort and NetworkLayer send helpers, keep non-SC transports on default ignore-on-send behavior, and encode SC DataAttribute values as Data Options while validating option type 1..31, the 64-option cap, and u16 option-data lengths before writing the BVLC-SC frame. Router tests cover forwarded unicast, forwarded broadcast, and loopback SC-to-SC forwarding preserving Data Options on the outbound SC frame. Remaining work is native send-path enforcement of the Secure Path type-1 marker constraints (to_data_options accepts a type-1 option without Must Understand and with a payload; the only prior evidence for those constraints was a removed non-native build path), high-level helper address-resolution/target-VMAC behavior, and formal conformance-test evidence.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC initiating and accepting peers enforce connection-state transitions, Connect-Accept response correlation, disconnect final-message behavior, and duplicate-VMAC collision signaling.
rows.notes: AB-03 adds native Connect-Accept message-id matching evidence, preserves the Connecting state when a pure state-machine response does not match the pending Connect-Request, and makes the async native handshake fail/disconnect on a mismatched response. Native Connect-Accept handling now requires the fixed AB.2.11.1 26-byte payload before entering Connected, stores peer Max-BVLC-Length and Max-NPDU-Length, advertises local Max-BVLC-Length, rejects outbound NPDUs or encoded BVLC frames that exceed peer limits, and discards oversized inbound WebSocket payloads before BVLC processing. The hub stores client Max-BVLC-Length and Max-NPDU-Length from Connect-Request, advertises its own limits in Connect-Accept, rejects non-26-byte Connect-Request payloads, drops inbound frames above the hub limit before decode, and filters unicast/broadcast relay targets by each recipient's negotiated NPDU and encoded BVLC limits. The hub BVLC-Result NAK builder now takes typed BACnet ErrorClass/ErrorCode values; duplicate client or hub VMAC collisions are encoded as COMMUNICATION/NODE_DUPLICATE_VMAC (7/151) instead of raw 1/1, and known-but-invalid functions are no longer classified as BVLC_FUNCTION_UNKNOWN. AB-07 stores each hub client's Device UUID, accepts known-UUID Connect-Request replacements, sends a WebSocket Close to the superseded connection, wakes the superseded handler, keeps superseded sinks from relaying or removing the replacement entry, and revalidates both source and recipient closed tokens immediately before relay writes so marked-superseded sinks are not written after replacement wins. It also preserves NODE_DUPLICATE_VMAC NAK behavior for a new UUID that collides with an existing client or hub VMAC. Live generated-certificate WebSocket evidence now requires the superseded connection to receive a Close frame, rejects a second Connect-Request from an already connected client without replacing a peer that it claims, verifies the closed client's original VMAC is no longer reachable, verifies peer reachability after that invalid connected-state transition, and decodes duplicate-VMAC BVLC-Result NAK values at the WebSocket boundary. Transport receive-loop evidence now covers WebSocket close/error receive paths transitioning the native connection to Disconnected before exit, heartbeat send failures disconnecting before retry/exit, reconnect exhaustion leaving Disconnected, and oversized frame discard. Existing transport tests also cover connect timeout to Disconnected, Disconnect-Request construction, Disconnect-ACK transition from Disconnecting, and hub Device UUID payload parsing. This tranche adds Annex H.7.3 Random-48 VMAC generation, native Connect-Request BVLC-Result handling that detects COMMUNICATION/NODE_DUPLICATE_VMAC (7/151), requires the BVLC-Result message ID to match the pending Connect-Request before reseeding, disconnects, clears the pending connect, and installs a new Random-48 VMAC before later attempts. Native duplicate-VMAC reseed failure now blocks failover/retry eligibility so a stale duplicate VMAC is not sent on a subsequent failover Connect-Request. Failed primary-restore probes now copy a successful Random-48 reseed or fail-closed retry-block state back to the active connection before the probe is discarded, preventing later primary-restore or reconnect attempts from reusing a stale duplicate VMAC. Native connect-time failures now clear the pending Connect-Request on timeouts, invalid Connect-Accept responses, malformed BVLC-Result wires, generic SC decode errors, and WebSocket send/receive I/O errors. It also adds failover and primary-restore evidence that retry Connect-Requests use the reselected VMAC, primary-restore reseed-failure evidence that no stale-VMAC retry is sent, generic and wrong-message-id Connect-Request NAK evidence that does not reseed. Remaining AB.6.2 gaps include explicit AWAITING_WEBSOCKET modeling at the WebSocket adapter boundary, accepting-peer connect-wait timeout, Disconnect wait behavior in ScTransport::stop, and reserved VMAC error signaling.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC hub connector, hub relay behavior, VMAC routing, disconnect, and failover behavior are validated.
rows.notes: AB-06 adds hub connector/forwarding evidence for Annex AB.5.3.2, AB.5.3.3, and AB.5.4. Hub-bound Encapsulated-NPDU messages now carry Destination Virtual Address and omit Originating Virtual Address; local receive logic accepts hub-relayed unicast with no Destination Virtual Address and drops non-broadcast Destination Virtual Address from hub relay. The hub rejects forwarding attempts with an Originating Virtual Address or missing Destination Virtual Address, selects only the matching VMAC for unicast, discards unknown unicast destinations by producing no recipient, fans broadcast to all current hub connections except the origin, preserves Message ID/payload/destination options/data options, adds the sender Originating Virtual Address, strips Destination Virtual Address for unicast forwarding, and preserves broadcast Destination Virtual Address for broadcast forwarding. Live generated-certificate WebSocket evidence covers three connected clients: A-to-B unicast reaches only B with the required VMAC transformation and option preservation, A-to-unknown unicast reaches no client, and A broadcast reaches B and C but not A while preserving the broadcast Destination Virtual Address. AB-07 adds live generated-certificate WebSocket evidence that a known Device UUID replacement moves hub reachability to the replacement VMAC, prevents old-VMAC unicast delivery, requires a Close frame for the superseded connection, prevents marked-superseded source or recipient sinks from relaying after replacement wins, and preserves peer reachability after rejecting a connected client's second Connect-Request. Transport connector evidence now covers initial primary timeout to failover, established primary loss with reconnect exhaustion, failover Connect-Request/Connect-Accept, connection state update, active unicast send-path swap to the failover hub, and primary restoration while failover is active. Primary restoration uses a separate probe connection, sends a best-effort Disconnect-Request to the failover hub after the primary Connect-Accept succeeds, swaps the active transport path back to the primary hub, and verifies subsequent unicast traffic is sent to the restored primary. This slice adds relay helper and live generated-certificate WebSocket evidence that 31 minimum-size Destination Options plus 31 minimum-size Data Options remain within the 1476-byte BVLC size budget and are preserved through hub unicast relay; helper coverage also verifies broadcast preservation with the same option chains. This slice also adds explicit unsupported direct-connection classification evidence: the hub WebSocket subprotocol selection rejects `dc.bsc.bacnet.org`, and a connected hub client sending Address-Resolution receives a BVLC-Result NAK with COMMUNICATION/UNEXPECTED_DATA rather than BVLC_FUNCTION_UNKNOWN. Configured hub URI evidence covers the production TlsWebSocket::connect parse boundary preserving the configured wss authority, port, path, and query before dialing; malformed or hostless configured hub URIs are rejected before any WebSocket/TLS dial. ASHRAE Addendum cc to 135-2020 changes AB.5.3.1 hub-connection metadata and Network Port properties but does not change these forwarding, replacement, reconnect-failover, option-preservation, configured/malformed hub URI, or direct-connection unsupported-classification behaviors. No remaining hub connector gaps are tracked in this row.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC WebSocket subprotocol, binary frames, wss/TLS, TLS 1.3, and mutual TLS expectations are enforced or explicitly limited.
rows.notes: AB-04 adds native WebSocket evidence for configured-peer URI scheme rejection before dialing unless the scheme is wss, native initiating-peer verification that the selected hub subprotocol is hub.bsc.bacnet.org, accepting-hub rejection of missing/wrong subprotocol offers, successful real TLS WebSocket hub subprotocol negotiation, and real TLS WebSocket text-frame close with status 1003. Native and hub adapters already send BVLC-SC payloads as binary WebSocket frames and ignore Ping/Pong as optional WebSocket control traffic. AB-05 adds TLS 1.3-only native Python hub configuration, TLS 1.3-only benchmark/test helper configuration, generated-certificate evidence for valid mTLS, missing client certificate, wrong client issuer, expired/not-yet-valid client and server certificates, wrong server SAN, malformed PEM, mismatched cert/key pairs, explicit TLS 1.3 negotiation, and TLS 1.2-only client rejection. The benchmark SC hub now enforces client certificates when --ca is supplied. Direct WebSocket connections using dc.bsc.bacnet.org remain deferred/unsupported because direct connections are not implemented or publicly claimed. The combined AB.7 row remains implementation-present-needs-security-tests until TLS 1.3 application profile/cipher-suite evidence, revocation behavior when configured, production file-path helper tests, and any optional certificate identity policy are fully evidenced; server-auth-only examples remain documented as non-conformant example/benchmark mode.

rows.requirement_summary: BACnet/SC heartbeat request/ack behavior, timeout range, disconnect, and retry behavior are validated.
rows.notes: AB.6.3 heartbeat evidence now covers no-VMAC Heartbeat-Request/Heartbeat-ACK construction, native Heartbeat-ACK message-id/no-VMAC validation, production `ScTransport::start` rejection of configurable heartbeat intervals outside 3..300 seconds, production rejection of disconnect timeouts that are not greater than the heartbeat interval, periodic heartbeat initiation after idle inbound BVLC activity, inbound BVLC activity resetting the liveness timer, timeout-driven native disconnect when no BVLC response arrives, send-error disconnect behavior, and hub-initiated heartbeat tracking that sends idle Heartbeat-Requests, records the pending Message ID, clears the pending state only for a matching Heartbeat-ACK, and removes the hub client when the pending ACK exceeds the hub timeout. Accelerated native heartbeat tests use a private test-only timing override so production builders keep Annex AB.6.3 range enforcement at start. The row remains open because the native heartbeat timeout evidence relies on a test-only timing override rather than formal Annex AB.6.3 timeout conformance tests.
